subject: Scope of default capture for interactive streams and generated artifacts

Subject: Clarify what Redwood stores by default (streams, prompts, outputs)

Hi Sergio,

We're finishing procurement for our Redwood pilot and the security team has a handful of specific questions about the default capture/retention behaviour. Can you confirm the following for hosted Redwood accounts (EU region):

- Do you store streamed tokens (partial generation) by default, or only final responses?
- Are function call outputs / tool responses treated as "outputs" (longer retention) or as part of the request?
- How are embeddings stored by default and for how long?
- Is the KV/prefix cache ever persisted to disk or to customer-visible logs?
- What is the standard deletion path if we request erasure (self-serve API vs support ticket), and typical SLA to complete?

This will be part of our vendor questionnaire; a short written summary we can attach to the procurement file would be helpful.

Thanks,

Hi all — adding more concrete detail below so BrightPath can drop this into procurement. TL;DR: defaults optimized for reliability/diagnostics; erasure path available for hosted customers.

1) Streamed tokens vs final responses
- Default: Redwood captures the full request (user inputs, structured fields, and metadata) and final model outputs by default.
- Streamed partial tokens (intermediate chunks) are not persisted to long-term logs unless the customer's account has streaming_capture enabled (opt-in feature for diagnostics). When streaming_capture is enabled, the stream fragments are treated as request artifacts and retained under the same window as requests (see #3).

2) Function/tool call outputs
- Function call payloads and tool responses are classified as generated outputs. They are stored as part of the session output bundle and retained under the outputs retention window. We treat them as "generated artifacts" rather than raw requests because they may include downstream tool data.

3) Retention windows (hosted, default settings)
- Requests (prompts, form fields, and request metadata): retained for 30 days.
- Generated outputs (model answers, function-call results, tool responses): retained for 90 days.
- Embeddings and indexed artifacts: retained 365 days by default (these are considered long-lived by product).
- KV / prefix cache: ephemeral in hosted deployments — kept in-memory and persisted to local node caches for up to 48 hours for performance; not written to long-term logs. Dedicated/Private customers can configure persistence.

4) Residency
- For accounts in the EU region we keep data in EU regions by default (control plane metadata may still reach US control endpoints for billing/ops telemetry under strict pseudonymization — we can provide the control-plane flow diagram if needed).

5) Deletion / erasure paths
- Self-serve: Customers can request bulk erasure via the Console (Data > Erase) for eligible items; API erase endpoints are in public docs (we can include sample calls).
- Support-assisted: For cases requiring deeper trace removal (e.g., tombstones, index re-references), open a support ticket — typical SLA is 3–7 business days to complete the hosted erasure depending on scope.
- Dedicated/Private: Customers manage storage and erasure for on-prem/Dedicated deployments; Redwood provides runbooks and support.

6) Attachments and binary blobs
- Attachments referenced by requests (e.g., uploaded files) are stored in object storage tied to the account and follow the same retention policy as the parent request unless explicitly uploaded to a long-term artifact store (embeddings/indexes).

7) Auditability and proof for procurement
- We can provide a signed vendor statement covering the above, plus a sample erasure report from a prior request (redacted). If BrightPath wants a deeper control-plane diagram and the SOC-2 artifact timeline, we can attach those.

Happy to revise wording for procurement.

—Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
